correctness.rationale: Both base words of 9 and 16 characters are checked against all 32 binary length-five strings; the r>=2 base follows by a monotone scattered embedding. The decomposition W_{r,k+1}=A 0^H A doubles binary subsequence universality. Any absent length-(2m+1) pattern must have both length-(m+1) overlapping halves absent from A; a complete overlap enumeration yields two possible middle symbols (r>=2) or five middle triples (r=1). All zero-centered candidates embed via the two m-universal copies. A first/last-one count proves exactly the surviving four or nine candidates absent. The proof is an induction for every r>=1,k>=2. An independent pair of sequence constructions and an exact earliest-position automaton dynamic program output VERIFY_OK on 24 nontrivial sample pairs. Finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The 2015 Cantor-like substitution paper concerns permutation/contiguous factor complexity, not complete shortest absent scattered-subsequence sets. The full text of the 2021 absent-subsequence preprint develops general notions and algorithms, without a Cantor-like generation-by-generation classification. Generic published finite-length distributions and unrestricted extremal enumerations do not fix the forbidden sets for a given morphic word. Comparisons of accessible Cantor-specific earlier claims involve rotation classes, 2-binomial factor classes, and initial repeated contiguous factors; these do not imply scattered-subsequence absence. No covering source appeared in targeted database or literature queries; this is a best-knowledge conclusion, not a uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: The general family of Cantor-like morphisms is canonical in automatic combinatorics on words, and shortest absent subsequences / universality are natural complexity invariants. This is an all-parameter exact classification, not an arbitrary finite slice: the complete shortest forbidden sets remain exactly nine or four while the universal length grows as 2^k. The sharp r=1 versus r>=2 structural transition is not recoverable from generic arch bounds; the two-forbidden-halves inductive mechanism can inform other self-similar word questions. It does not claim broader statements for arbitrary factors or all minimal absent patterns.
